recipes.name: LAST-MINUTE THANKSGIVING
ingredients: duck fat, softened (room temperature), as needed
1 cup sugar plus more as needed (adjust for tartness)
1 package of bacon, thick cut (not extra thick)
instructions: For Upside Down Roasted Chicken:
For optional dry brine, rinse and pat dry the chicken. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken
Place the chicken on a rimmed baking sheet with an inlaid grilling rack. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken
Cover the exterior of the chicken with a light coating of salt and pepper. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken - kosher salt as needed - freshly ground pepper as needed
Keep uncovered and refrigerated overnight or up to 24 hours. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken
Preheat the oven to 425°F.

Using your hand, gently separate the skin from the chicken meat without tearing it. Spread a thin layer of duck fat underneath the skin. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken - duck fat softened (room temperature), as needed

Coat the bird in another layer of duck fat over the skin. Sprinkle it with salt and pepper. (make sure to get in all of the nooks and crannies) - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken - duck fat softened (room temperature), as needed - kosher salt as needed - freshly ground pepper as needed
Tie the thighs together using butcher’s twine or gauze (truss the bird). - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken
Fill the cavity with half of the thyme, lemon, and garlic. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken - 12 thyme sprigs divided - ½ lemon - 1 head of garlic halved
Place the chicken breast-side down on a large skillet. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken
Add onions and remaining thyme to fill the rest of the pan. - 1 onion roughly sliced - 12 thyme sprigs divided
Bake for 30 minutes. Remove the chicken from the oven and carefully flip the bird breast-side up. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken

Return the pan to the oven and cook for another 30 minutes or until the thickest part of the chicken thigh registers 175°F and the breast skin is a deep golden brown. (If the meat is done but the skin needs more browning, turn the oven to broil for 3-5 minutes). - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken

Remove the onions and the rendered fat from the pan, but keep the stuck-on fond in the pan. Reserve the fat in a separate bowl. - 1 onion roughly sliced - duck fat softened (room temperature), as needed
Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes before carving. - 1 (4 to 6 lbs) whole chicken
For Cranberry Sauce:

Combine all ingredients, save for water, in a medium saucepan. - 1 cup sugar plus more as needed (adjust for tartness) - 1 bag cranberries - Gran Marnier a splash - 1 orange sliced peel and juice - 1 stick cinnamon - knob of ginger crushed
Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until thick, bubbly, and the cranberries have burst.

Taste for tartness (add sugar if needed), remove orange peel, ginger knob, and cinnamon stick. - 1 orange sliced peel and juice - 1 stick cinnamon - knob of ginger crushed - 1 cup sugar plus more as needed (adjust for tartness)
Add water if the mixture is too thick and continue to cook for another 15 minutes. Let cool. - water as needed
Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to use.
For Brussels Sprouts:
Slice brussels sprouts in half and place in a large bowl. - 2 lbs Brussels sprouts
Toss with olive oil, salt, and pepper - 2 lbs Brussels sprouts - olive oil as needed - kosher salt as needed - freshly ground pepper as needed
Spread Brussels sprouts in an even layer on a baking sheet cut side down. - 2 lbs Brussels sprouts
Lay strips of bacon across the sprouts. - 2 lbs Brussels sprouts - 1 package of bacon thick cut (not extra thick)
Cover and refrigerate until ready to cook. - 2 lbs Brussels sprouts - 1 package of bacon thick cut (not extra thick)
Bake at 425°F for 30-35 minutes. - 2 lbs Brussels sprouts - 1 package of bacon thick cut (not extra thick)
If the bacon isn’t crisp but the Brussels sprouts are done, remove the sprouts and cook the bacon for an additional 5-10 minutes.
Once cooled enough to handle, chop bacon into small pieces and toss with the Brussels sprouts. - 1 package of bacon thick cut (not extra thick) - 2 lbs Brussels sprouts
For Apple Crumble Tart:
For the Crust
Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Combine flour, sugar, salt, and melted butter in a bowl. - 10 oz flour - 4 oz sugar - 1 tsp salt - 15 tbsp butter melted
Press 2/3 of the dough mixture into the sides and bottom of a tart pan. - For the Crust
Bake the crust for 20 minutes. Let cool. - For the Crust
For the Filling

Combine all ingredients (save for the apples and butter) in a large bowl. - 1 cup brown sugar packed - 2 tbsp Corn starch - 2 tsp. cinnamon - 1 tsp. allspice - 1 ¼ clove - ½ tsp. cardamom - 1 tsp. kosher salt
Add apples and fold to combine. - 5 ½ medium Granny Smith apples sliced
In a large skillet, heat butter on medium heat. - 2 tbsp butter
Add the apple mixture and cook until the apples are tender (about 10 minutes). Let cool and reserve. - For the Filling
For the Topping
With the remaining 1/3 dough, add flour and sugar. Hand mix until just combined. Reserve until ready to use. - ⅓ cup remaining crust dough - 1 tbsp flour - 1 tbsp sugar
For assembly, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Pour apple filling over the baked crust and top with the crumbled dough. - For the Filling - For the Crust - For the Topping
Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown on top.
For Stuffing:
For the Croutons
Cut bread into 1/2 inch cubes. - 1 large loaf of sourdough bread
Spread across an even layer across two baking sheets - For the Croutons
Bake at 200°F for 1.5 hours or until fully crisp. Let cool. - For the Croutons
For the Sausage

Combine ingredients in a bowl. (Optional: refrigerate sausage meat overnight or until ready to cook stuffing) - For the Sausage - 1 lb ground pork - ½ tsp garlic - ½ onion - 1 tbsp minced sage - 1 tsp kosher salt - 1 tsp freshly ground pepper
For the Stuffing Assembly
In a large Dutch oven, heat oil on medium-high heat. - 1 tbsp neutral oil
Add pork, stir occasionally to break apart any large chunks. - Pork Sausage Mixture
Cook until browned on all sides. - Pork Sausage Mixture
Remove pork using a slotted spoon and reserve. - Pork Sausage Mixture
Melt butter and add onion, carrots, and celery to the Dutch oven and cook until tender (about 10 minutes). - 3 tbsp butter unsalted - ½ onion chopped - 2 carrots chopped - 2 celery stalks chopped
Meanwhile, begin heating turkey stock in a small saucepan. - 4 cups turkey broth
Add thyme, sage, and garlic and cook until fragrant. Add 1/2 cup of stock if the mixture gets too dry. - 1 tbsp thyme leaves chopped - 1 ½ tbsp sage chopped - 1 clove garlic - 4 cups turkey broth
Return sausage to the Dutch oven, add chestnuts and croutons, stir to combine. - Pork Sausage Mixture - 1 cup chestnuts chopped - For the Croutons
Add enough stock to moisten the bread. - 4 cups turkey broth
Gently fold ingredients and season with salt and pepper to taste. - kosher salt as needed - freshly ground pepper as needed
Turn off the heat and cover. Allow to sit for at least 10 minutes.
Once the chicken is out of the oven, place the covered Dutch oven in the oven for 7-10 minutes to crisp the stuffing.
For Pan Gravy:
Heat oil in a large pot, add chicken neck and onion and cook until chicken is browned on both sides and onions are tender. - 1 tbsp neutral oil - 1 chicken neck - ½ onion quartered (with skin)

Add celery leaves, carrots, thyme, sage, peppercorns, bay leaf, and turkey stock. Bring to a simmer and allow to cook until stock is reduced by 1/2 volume. - 1 bunch celery leaves - 2 carrots halved - 4 sprigs of thyme - 5 sage leaves - 1 tbsp black peppercorns - 1 bay leaf dried - 1 (32 oz) carton turkey stock
Using the pot from cooking the chicken, add butter, flour, and saved chicken fat to make a roux. - 1 tbsp reserved fat from chicken - 2 tbsp butter unsalted - 3 tbsp all purpose flour
Add in reserved boosted turkey stock until sired thickness and then cook for 5 minutes over medium heat. - 1 (32 oz) carton turkey stock
Season to taste with salt and pepper. - kosher salt as needed - black pepper as needed
Reserve.
For Mashed Potatoes:
Peel and cut potatoes into 1/2 inch cubes. - Yukon gold potatoes
Place potatoes in a large high-sided skillet and fill with cold water until the potatoes are completely covered. - Yukon gold potatoes - water to cover
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Once boiling, cook for 15-20 minutes, until fork-tender (no resistance when prodded by a fork or pairing knife). - Yukon gold potatoes
Drain and mash potatoes with a masher in the same high-sided skillet. - Yukon gold potatoes
In a medium saucepan, melt butter over medium-high heat. Once frothy, add the garlic and cook until fragrant (about 3 minutes). - 1 stick (8 tbsp.) butter - 2 cloves garlic minced
Slowly add the cream and cook until warmed through. - 1 cup cream
Add cream mixture to the mashed potatoes and stir with a wood or plastic spatula.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. - kosher salt as needed - black pepper as needed
Keep warm until ready to serve, or refrigerate and reheat the next day.
